title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i].

The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.

You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and without using the division operation.

examples.explanation: Every position except the zero's own index includes the 0 in its product, so only answer[2] = -1*1*-3*3 = 9 is nonzero.

constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.

solution.python:
from typing import List


class Solution:
    def productExceptSelf(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        answer = [1] * n

        prefix = 1
        for i in range(n):
            answer[i] = prefix
            prefix *= nums[i]

        suffix = 1
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            answer[i] *= suffix
            suffix *= nums[i]

        return answer

approach: On a left-to-right pass, answer[i] stores the product of all elements strictly before i. A right-to-left pass then keeps one scalar suffix product and multiplies it into answer[i], extending the suffix with nums[i] afterwards. No division or zero-specific branching is needed. Time complexity is O(n). Auxiliary space is O(1) when the required output array is excluded; the returned array itself uses O(n) space.
